issues.description: StockIngredient's name getter is inconsistent between template and solution: the template defines getIngredientName(), while the solution (and its Stock.findStockIngredient implementation) uses getName(). If students implement Stock.findStockIngredient according to the intended API/solution, it will not compile against the template's StockIngredient without renaming or adding an adapter method.
issues.suggestedFix: Standardize the getter name to match the class diagram/solution: rename template StockIngredient.getIngredientName() to getName() and update template Stock.findStockIngredient accordingly; alternatively, keep getIngredientName() but add a getName() method delegating to it.

issues.description: The problem statement/UML for Stock lists only add, take, findStockIngredient, addToStockIngredients, and emptyStock, but the template additionally exposes a public setStockIngredients(StockIngredient[]) mutator. This extra public API contradicts the stated focus on getters for encapsulation and can confuse students about what the intended/graded Stock interface is.
issues.suggestedFix: Either document setStockIngredients(...) in the UML/spec as an allowed helper (e.g., for manual testing), or remove it from the template and adjust Main accordingly; if kept, consider making it package-private to reduce API surface.
